Effects of Estrogen: The degenerating corpus luteum stops producing estrogen, causing instability in the endometrium.
Effects of Progesterone: As the corpus luteum degenerates, it becomes nonfunctional and stops producing hormones. The level of progesterone falls. The endometrium becomes unstable.
Effects of FSH: The decrease in progesterone reduces the negative feedback, and the amount of the follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) can start re-increasing, preparing for the next menstrual cycle.
Effects of LH: The amount of the Luteinizing hormone (LH) remains low, but the decreasing amount of progesterone removes the negative feedback, preparing the next menstrual cycle.
Energy Levels Info: Due to the estrogen and progesterone suppressing gluconeogenesis your body will burn fat and not sugar, but this will make exercise feel harder. Due to this you will feel lower in energy and get tired quicker. It is recommended to do lower intensity workouts and strength sessions.
What to eat: During this phase it is best to eat carbs and proteins, as when doing exercise it will make your body rely on glucose less. Foods rich with vitamin B and healthy fats will also help to support hormonal balance, and therefore are recommended.
Foods and Recipes: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration: Through the luteal phase, the dynamic complexity of the brain remains high but the activity patterns change. This supports deeper thinking, reflection and social sensitivity. For this time it is best to focus on work that requires close attention to detail, deep thinking, and planning.
Health: The luteal phase normally does not vary in length. If your luteal phase is 10 days or less it is recommended you go talk to a specialist as there is a possibility that you may experience Luteal phase deficiency (LPD). Some possible symptoms include spotting, short cycle, and >10 day luteal phase. This disease may contribute to infertility and lead to miscarriages.
Mood: The change in the hormones will result in mood swings, irritation and symptoms of PMS. During this time you might feel sad, angry and easily irritated. You might also feel more overwhelmed and less sociable.
Types of Vitamins: During the luteal phase the best vitamins and supplements to take consist of Vitamin B6, magnesium and zinc. Vitamin B6 will help reduce premenstrual symptoms and support hormonal balance. As well as zinc contributing to help support hormonal balance. The magnesium will help to reduce bloating and regulate mood swings.
Insights in the Brain: If pregnancy did not occur, the level of progesterone falls. The negative feedback it had on the anterior pituitary is removed and the level of the Luteinizing hormone (LH) and the Follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) starts rising again, preparing the body for the next menstrual cycle.
Insights in the Ovaries: The corpus luteum degenerates into the corpus albicans, which is nonfunctional and does not produce hormones anymore. The level of progesterone and estrogens rapidly decreases.
Insights in the Uterus: The decreasing level of progesterone and estrogen creates instabilities in the endometrium.
Phase Info: If pregnancy did not occur, the corpus luteum transitions into a nonfunctional structure, the corpus albicans. The level of progesterone and estrogen rapidly drops, destabilizing the endometrium.
Today's Recap: Today you might start feeling tired and experiencing pre menstruation symptoms. At this time you may still feel reflective and have social sensitivity. You might experience of mood swings and feel irritated.
